h1: AI Designer Portfolio — Agencies & Studios Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference for an agency or studio, captured at 604x476 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Hero section reference for an agency or studio — cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) easing, 0.1s transitions, a stats row and a moving marquee.
about: AI Designer Portfolio is a working reference for an agency or studio: the hero section laid out, measured and ready to rebuild. The palette runs white #F6FCFF underneath and deep teal #051A24 for the type, and the type is Neue Montreal. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 604x476 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The page keeps its motion to 0.1s transitions, cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 11,458-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: Navigation is a single row with no second level under it. The bar sits over the 604x476 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: The sizes are in the brief, not in a scale
layout.body: The brief fixes type from 22px to 80px, 40px spacing steps, 0.1s transitions and cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) easing and leaves the rest to the arrangement, which is the opposite of a scale that grows on its own. The frame proportions are recorded with the sizes, so a rebuild gets the aspect right as well.

layout.title: Scanning beats reading here
layout.body: The grid does the reading order for you: panels of equal weight, one idea each, set in Neue Montreal at a small size so the structure stays visible. The grid collapses to a single column without changing the panel order. One idea per panel.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: A slim bar sits over the hero section with the wordmark on the left and the links set in Neue Montreal, so the composition reads as content first and chrome second.

motion.title: Hover, but sparingly
motion.body: The pointer work is small and specified: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card and a slider that pages through content on demand, applied to the elements that already look interactive. Nothing on the page opens a modal or hijacks the scroll; the interactions stay local to the element. Fewer states, fully specified.

motion.title: A marquee carries the rhythm
motion.body: A marquee runs across the composition on an endless loop, set in Neue Montreal, so the page has movement even where nothing animates on scroll. Because the strip is decorative, it can be paused or dropped without changing the layout.

notes: The display line is Neue Montreal at the top of a 22–80px scale, with the interface text on the same face.
Media is specified at 604x476 and a 17.2s loop, so a replacement should match the crop and the loop length.
Nothing sits between the type and the 604x476 clip, so a replacement has to work under the copy directly.

customize: The brief behind this page is written out in full below, so any rewrite can be checked against it value by value; the reference was captured at 604x476.
Retime the entrance to taste. 0.1s with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) is what the reference uses.
Keep Neue Montreal or pick a face with the same proportions; the size scale is set for those widths, not for a substitute.
Replace the video with a still at 604x476 if the 17.2s loop is too heavy for the page you are shipping.

editorial.title: The timing behind the hero section
editorial.body: Every transition here has a number attached. That is why 0.1s transitions, a 17.2s media loop and a scroll reveal can be ported value by value instead of re-tuned by feel. Nothing animates for its own sake in this hero section.

editorial.title: What this hero section gets right
editorial.body: Most agency pages add another section when the first screen is weak. This one removes options instead: navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the card grid, in that order, and nothing that repeats the offer. It gives a agency reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: Reading AI Designer Portfolio as a spec
editorial.body: Specific numbers age: a value that suits 604x476 may not suit your frame. The brief states type from 22px to 80px and 40px spacing steps anyway, because a stated value is easier to change than an unstated one. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

faq.question: Is the AI Designer Portfolio prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 604x476, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: How much of AI Designer Portfolio depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: AI Designer Portfolio was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Where did the AI Designer Portfolio design come from?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 604x476.
